evidence: harness/provenance/listener.py has never decoded wire bytes (git log -S read_exact returns nothing)
wire decoding lives in harness/untrusted_peer, where naive.py:25 is the unbounded site
the analyzer reported no length finding for listener.py, which is the correct result
limitations: the analyzer cannot distinguish a stale report from a missed detection from the text alone
next_action: Keep the pattern fixture where the pattern lives; assert the listener never decodes bytes.
observed: A report placed a peer-controlled length reaching read_exact at this line. The line reads env.origin == REMOTE and msg.get('origin') == INTERNAL, the file contains no read_exact and no struct.unpack, and git log -S read_exact over that file is empty.
root_cause: a finding located by module name rather than by the site that performs the read
why_matters: A finding filed against a site that cannot contain the defect teaches nothing and spends review attention on the wrong file, while the site that does contain it goes unexamined.

evidence: reproduction R63 fails the old rule and passes the new one
only min() against a constant or a named limit caps a size now
limitations: the rule proves no bound is visible, not that none exists
next_action: Test every clamp the rule credits in both directions.
observed: The size rule treated max() and min() alike when deciding whether a wire-derived length was bounded, so size = max(peer_length, 1) produced no finding.
root_cause: a floor mistaken for a ceiling in the analyzer's model of bounds
why_matters: max() bounds a value from below. A peer still chooses the allocation, and the rule reported the worst input as safe.

evidence: reproduction R64 fails the old rule and passes the new one
a guard now counts only when its body raises, returns, breaks or continues
limitations: crediting is whole-scope once one guard exits, so a use before the guard is not modelled
path-sensitivity beyond a single guard is out of reach for this analysis
next_action: Keep the rejecting and non-rejecting forms as a permanent pair.
observed: Any comparison between a wire-derived name and a limit marked that name as bounded, so 'if n < MAX_FRAME: pass' followed by read_exact(n) produced no finding.
root_cause: the same assumption as SR-BOUND-001: a syntactic marker read as a semantic guarantee
why_matters: Presence of a comparison is not evidence of a check. A guard that rejects nothing leaves the peer in control of the size, and the rule credited it anyway.

evidence: reproduction R60 fails the old rule and passes the new one
safe() and unsafe() sharing a variable name is now a regression test
limitations: analysis remains intraprocedural: a value passed into a function is not followed
next_action: Apply the same scoping test to every rule that collects names.
observed: Denominator floors were collected module-wide, so a floor assigned inside one function protected an unfloored division inside another.
root_cause: names collected without regard to the scope that owns them
why_matters: A false negative in a high rule is silent. Nothing prompts anyone to look at the code the rule failed to report.

evidence: two occurrences in listener.py now require two entries with two reasons
stale and ambiguous entries fail the run instead of passing quietly
limitations: a fingerprint tracks a line of text, so reformatting the line invalidates the exemption and fails the build deliberately
next_action: Require every exemption to name one occurrence.
observed: Exemptions were keyed on path and rule, so one entry suppressed every occurrence of that rule in that file, including occurrences added later with different intent.
root_cause: a suppression keyed at a coarser grain than the reason that justified it
why_matters: The written reason described one case while the suppression covered all of them, and two opposite-intent reads of a claimed origin shared a single entry.

evidence: the ignore rule excluded harness/self_review_allow.txt from every commit
the one path is now un-ignored explicitly
the exact expected exemption set is asserted in a test, so the file's contents are checked even if it goes missing
limitations: the pipeline notices a missing file that changes a result, not one that silently matches nothing
next_action: Assert that every file the review depends on is tracked by git.
observed: The exemption list was matched by the *.txt ignore rule, so it existed on the development machine and never reached CI. Local runs were clean and CI found four high findings.
root_cause: an ignore pattern protecting against committed document bodies also matched a configuration file
why_matters: A control that reports success because it was never exercised is worse than an absent control, since it manufactures confidence.

evidence: the self-review reports all three as low findings on every run
limitations: consolidation is a design change, not a defect fix, and the self-review cannot tell a deliberate local constant from an oversight
next_action: Consolidate the thresholds into one policy manifest and have the rules read from it.
observed: Three defensive thresholds are declared in three separate modules: MAX_HOPS in listener.py, MAX_WALL_SECONDS and MAX_FRAMES_PER_CONNECTION in protocol.py.
why_matters: Policy that lives where it is used cannot be inspected, compared or changed in one place, and a missing limit is invisible because there is no list to be missing from.

evidence: harness/untrusted_peer/alias_chain.py now holds both halves of the pattern
R66 drives the naive half into a 2 GB allocation and the guarded half into a refusal after four bytes
limitations: a fixture proves the rule and runtime agree about this shape, not that the shape is exhaustive
next_action: Add a fixture whenever a defect class arrives from outside with no in-repo counterpart.
observed: No repository fixture carried a peer-controlled length through two aliases before reaching an allocation, so alias handling was tested only against inline snippets.
root_cause: defect classes entered through review rather than through the acquisition pipeline
why_matters: A rule's alias handling was unverified against real code while appearing covered by unit tests written to match the rule's own behaviour.

evidence: the five-link chain taints fully in one source-ordered pass
a chain needing two passes requires using a name before assigning it, which is not valid in that shape
the chain is caught under a three-pass budget in a direct check
limitations: a fixed budget could still bite once a loop or a reordering appears, which is why iteration is now a fixpoint anyway
next_action: Keep fixpoint iteration as a hardening change; file no defect without a failing reproduction.
observed: A review reported that a three-pass propagation budget let a five-link alias chain escape detection.
root_cause: a plausible mechanism asserted without executing the example
why_matters: Acting on it as a defect would have added a reproduction that does not fail against the old code, which is how a corpus fills with tests that assert nothing.
